purpose: Unify the hunter into one identity-preserving sprite sheet with grounded standing poses and eight-frame directional cycles.
prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production sprite sheet for a top-down 2D pixel-art action game.
Input image 1 is the identity reference only: preserve this hooded female hunter's dark purple hood and short cape, burgundy scarf, small pale face with red eyes, brown boots and belt, small orange belt charm. Simplify internal details and shading into clean readable pixel clusters. She must stay the same character across EVERY cell.
Primary request: replace the inconsistent animation with one cohesive professional sprite sheet, true transparent background. Exactly FIVE evenly spaced rows and NINE evenly spaced columns, no text, labels, grid, shadows, ground, weapons, glow or effects. Forty-five separate full-body sprites. All characters equal height, equal head/body ratio, centered at their hips, boots on a consistent baseline. Large transparent gutters so no sprites touch. Entire figure inside each cell.
ROW DIRECTIONS, top to bottom: 1 facing RIGHT (east, clear side view); 2 facing DOWN-RIGHT (southeast three-quarter front); 3 facing DOWN (south, front); 4 facing UP-RIGHT (northeast three-quarter back); 5 facing UP (north, back). Do not substitute the same direction in multiple rows.
COLUMN ORDER within every row: column 1 a relaxed grounded STANDING pose with both boots down and hands near waist; columns 2 through 9 are EIGHT consecutive equal-time phases of ONE COMPLETE looping WALK/JOG cycle in place. Specifically: left-leg forward contact, left-leg down/recoil, right-leg passing, right-leg high/passing forward, RIGHT-leg forward contact (opposite leg to column 2!), right-leg down/recoil, LEFT-leg passing, left-leg high/passing forward. Animate opposite legs, not the same front boot repeated. Alternating feet, clean planted soles, short compact strides, knees never tucked into a floating jump. Contact and opposite-contact poses clearly different. All five rows share exactly the same anatomical leg phase in each column. For south/north views one foot moves forward while the other moves back, then swaps.
Style: restrained 32-bit-era low-resolution pixel art, approx 40x56 logical pixels per character, crisp squared pixel edges, solid one-logical-pixel dark outline, about 14 solid colors, two-tone cloth shading, no smooth gradients, no antialiasing, no painterly rendering. Head and torso volume locked across all frames, no size changes or facial drift. Motion carried by feet, modest arm counter-swing and small delayed cape/scarf follow-through. Head bob no more than one logical pixel. Short cape must leave the boots readable in back views. Empty fists, front/right fist stable near waist to receive a separately rendered gun. Consistent lighting from upper left in every cell. Functional animation reference, not an illustration.
